resources.string: This proxy\'s address is shown here while the connection is open and for ten minutes after it ends. It is not logged, because \"Log where apps connect through your tool, WireGuard or a proxy\" is off.
Where the app asked the proxy to go is not shown or logged, because \"Log where apps connect through your tool, WireGuard or a proxy\" is off.

Through the %1$s. Its address is no longer shown: while \"Log where apps connect through your tool, WireGuard or a proxy\" is off, Datapavan shows a proxy\'s address only while the connection is open and for ten minutes after it ends.

Through the %1$s in Android\'s settings, which other apps can use too. Its address is no longer shown: while \"Log where apps connect through your tool, WireGuard or a proxy\" is off, Datapavan shows a proxy\'s address only while the connection is open and for ten minutes after it ends.

Off unless you turn it on. It covers the apps you send through your circumvention tool or a WireGuard configuration, and the tool\'s own servers. Datapavan still counts their connections. It also covers apps that connect through a proxy, such as a Telegram proxy. While it is off, Now shows the proxy\'s address while the connection is open and for ten minutes after, and Datapavan logs only that the app used a proxy, which kind, when, and facts that name no address, such as whether a password was sent unencrypted. A list of where they went can be used against you if someone searches your phone.
